questions.q: Let $P_n=\alpha^n+\beta^n, n \in \mathbf{N}$. If $P_{10}=123, P_9=76$, $P_8=47$ and $P_1=1$, then the quadratic equation having roots $\frac{1}{\alpha}$ and $\frac{1}{\beta}$ is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \alpha^{10}+\beta^{10}=123 \\ & \alpha+\beta=1 \\ & \alpha^9+\beta^9=76 \\ & \alpha^8+\beta^8=47 \\ & P_{10}=P_9+P_8 \\ & x^2=x+1 \Rightarrow x^2-x-1=0 \\ & \alpha+\beta=1, \alpha \beta=-1 \\ & \frac{1}{\alpha}+\frac{1}{\beta}=\frac{\alpha+\beta}{\alpha \beta}=\frac{1}{-1}=-1, \frac{1}{\alpha \beta}=-1\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}, a \ne 0$ be such that the equation, $ax^{2} - 2bx + 5 = 0$ has a repeated root $\alpha,$ which is also a root of the equation, $x^{2} - 2bx - 10 = 0 .$ If $\beta$ is the other root of this equation, then ${\alpha}^{2} + {\beta}^{2}$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,& $ax^{2} - 2bx + 5 = 0$~has repeated root~$\alpha$.

$∴ 2\alpha = \dfrac{2b}{a} ⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{b}{a}$and~${α}^{2} = \dfrac{5}{a} ⇒ \dfrac{b2}{a2} = \dfrac{5}{a}$

$⇒ b^{2} = 5a . . . \left(i\right)$~ \left(a \ne 0\right)$

$\alpha + \beta =2b . . . \left(ii\right)$

and $\alpha\beta = -10 . . . \left($iii\right)$

\alpha = $\dfrac{b}{a}$is also root of $x^{2} - 2bx - 10 = 0$

$⇒ b^{2} - 2ab^{2} - 10a^{2} = 0$

by \left($i\right)⇒ 5a - 10a^{2} - 10a^{2} = 0$

$⇒ 20a^{2} = 5a$

$⇒ a = \dfrac{1}{4}$and $b^{2} = \dfrac{5}{4}$

Now ${α}^{2} + {β}^{2} = \left(\alpha + \beta\right)$2 - $2\alpha\beta

$= 5 + 20$

$= 25$

$

questions.q: The probability of selecting integers $a \in  \left[-5, 30\right]$~such that $x^{2} + 2\left(a + 4\right)x - 5a + 64 > 0$, for all~$x \in \mathbb{R}, is:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have,

$x^{2} + 2\left(a + 4\right)x - 5a + 64 > 0$

If~$A > 0$~and~$D = B^{2} - 4AC < 0$, then~$Ax^{2} + Bx + C > 0 \forall x \in R$.

Hence,

$D < 0$

$⇒ 4\left(a + 4\right)2 - 4\left(- 5a + 64\right) < 0$

$⇒ a^{2} + 16 + 8a + 5a - 64 < 0$

$⇒ a^{2} + 13a - 48 < 0$

$⇒ \left(a + 16\right) \left($a - 3\right) < 0$

$⇒ a \in \left(- 16, 3\right)$

$∴$ Possible values for~$a$~are~\left\{- 15, - 14, \ldots \ldots . , 2\right\}$~containing~$18$~integers.

But given range of~$a$~is~ \left[- 5, 30\right]$, hence~$a$~would take values~ \left\{- 5, - 4, - 3, - 2, - 1, 0, 1, 2\right\}$, containing~$8$~integers.

And,~\left[- 5, 30\right]$~has~$36$~numbers.

$∴$ Required probability

$= \dfrac{8}{36}$

$= \dfrac{2}{9}$

$

questions.q: If& $\alpha, \beta$~are the roots of the equation~$x^{2} - \left(5 + {3}^{\log_{3}5} - {5}^{\log_{5}3}\right)x + 3\left({3}^{\left(\log_{3}5\right)\dfrac{1}{3}} - {5}^{\left(\log_{5}3\right)\dfrac{2}{3}} - 1\right) = 0$~then the equation, whose roots are~$\alpha + \dfrac{1}{β}$~and~$\beta + \dfrac{1}{α}$,
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given& $\alpha, \beta$~are the roots of the equation~$x^{2} - \left(5 + {3}^{\log_{3}5} - {5}^{\log_{5}3}\right)x + 3\left({3}^{\left(\log_{3}5\right)\dfrac{1}{3}} - {5}^{\left(\log_{5}3\right)\dfrac{2}{3}} - 1\right) = 0$

Now~${3}^{\log_{3}5} - {5}^{\log_{5}3} = {3}^{\log_{3}5} - \left({3}^{\log_{3}5}\right)\sqrt{\log_{5}3}$

$= {3}^{\log_{3}5} - {3}^{\log_{3}5} = 0$

Also~${3}^{\left(\log_{3}5\right)\dfrac{1}{3}} - {5}^{\left(\log_{5}3\right)\dfrac{2}{3}} = {5}^{\left(\log_{5}3\right)\dfrac{2}{3}} - {5}^{\left(\log_{5}3\right)\dfrac{2}{3}}$

$= 0$

So, given equation becomes~$x^{2} - 5x - 3 = 0$~

i.e. $\alpha + \beta = 5; \alpha\beta = - 3$

Now if the roots are~$\alpha + \dfrac{1}{β}$~and~$\beta + \dfrac{1}{α}$

i.e.,~$\dfrac{\alpha\beta + 1}{β} \text{ and } \dfrac{\alpha\beta + 1}{α}$~

i.e.,~$\dfrac{- 2}{β} \text{ and } \dfrac{- 2}{α}$

Then let~$\dfrac{- 2}{α} = t ⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{- 2}{t}$

As~${α}^{2} - 5\alpha - 3 = 0$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{- 2}{t}\right)2 - 5\left(\dfrac{- 2}{t}\right) - 3 = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{4}{t2} + \dfrac{10}{t} - 3 = 0$

$⇒ 3t^{2} - 10t - 4 = 0$

i.e.,~$3x^{2} - 10x - 4 = 0$& is the required equation.

questions.q: The number of solutions, of the equation $e^{\sin x} - 2e^{- \sin x} = 2$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let, $e^{\sin x} = t$

$⇒ t - \dfrac{2}{t} = 2$

$⇒ t^{2} - 2t - 2 = 0$

$⇒ t^{2} - 2t + 1 = 3$

$⇒ {\left(t - 1\right)}^{2} = 3$

$⇒ t = 1 \pm \sqrt{3}$

$⇒ t \approx 2 . 73, - 0 . 73\left(\text{not possible}\right)$

$⇒ t \approx 2 . 73$

$⇒ e^{\sin x} \approx 2 . 73$

$⇒ \sin x \approx \log_{e}\left(2 . 73\right)$

$⇒ \sin x > 1 \to \text{Not possible}$

So no solutions will be possible for the given equation.

questions.q: If $\alpha, \beta$ and $\gamma$ are three consecutive terms of a non-constant G.P. Such that the equations $\alphax^{2} + 2\betax + \gamma = 0$ and $x^{2} + x - 1 = 0$ have a common root, then $\alpha \left(\beta + \gamma\right)is equal to:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ are in G.P.$⇒ {β}^{2} = \alpha\gamma$
For the equation $\alphax^{2} + 2\betax + \gamma = 0$
$D = 4{\beta}^{2} - 4\alpha\gamma = 0$
Hence roots of the equation are equal and equals to $– \dfrac{\beta}{\alpha} = - \dfrac{\gamma}{\beta}$
Since given equation have common roots, hence $\dfrac{- \gamma}{\beta}$ must be a root of $x^{2} + x - 1 = 0$
$⇒ \dfrac{{\gamma}^{2}}{{\beta}^{2}} - \dfrac{\gamma}{\beta} - 1 = 0$
$⇒ {\gamma}^{2} - \gamma\beta - {\beta}^{2} = 0$
$⇒ {\gamma}^{2} = \beta \left(\beta + \gamma\right)$
$⇒ \gamma . $\dfrac{{\beta}^{2}}{\alpha} = \beta \left(\beta + \gamma\right)$
$⇒ $\alpha\left(\beta + \gamma\right) = \beta\gamma$

questions.q: The number of real roots of the equation $x\left|x\right| - 5\left|x + 2\right| + 6 = 0$, is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$x\left|x\right| - 5\left|x + 2\right| + 6 = 0$

Now taking case $\left(1\right)$ when $x < - 2$ we get,

$- x^{2} + 5x + 10 + 6 = 0$

$⇒ x^{2} - 5x - 16 = 0$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{5 - \sqrt{89}}{2}$, ignoring $x = \dfrac{5 + \sqrt{89}}{2}$ as $x < - 2$, so one solution is possible here,

Now taking case $\left(2\right)$ when $- 2 \le x < 0$ we get,

$- x^{2} - 5x - 10 + 6 = 0$

$⇒ x^{2} + 5x + 4 = 0$

$⇒ x = - 1$, ignoring $x = - 4$ as $- 2 \le x < 0$

Now taking case $\left(3\right)$, when $x \ge 0$ we get,

$x^{2} - 5x - 10 + 6 = 0$

$⇒ x^{2} - 5x - 4 = 0$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{5 + \sqrt{41}}{2}$, ignoring $x = \dfrac{5 - \sqrt{41}}{2}$ as $x \ge 0$

So, from all cases we get total $3$ solutions.

questions.q:
Let
$S = \left\{x: x \in \mathbb{R}\text{\text{ and }} \left(\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2}\right)x^{2} - 4 + \left(\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{2}\right)x^{2} - 4 = 10\}$. Then n \left($S\right)$ is equal to$$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given:

$S = \left\{x: \left(\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2}\right)x^{2} - 4 + \left(\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{2}\right)x^{2} - 4 = 10\right\}$

Now,

$\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{2} = \dfrac{\left(\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2}\right)\left(\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{2}\right)}{\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2}}$

So,

\left(\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2}\right)x^{2} - 4 + \left(\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{2}\right)x^{2} - 4 = 10$

$⇒ \left(\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2}\right)x^{2} - 4 + \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2}}\right)x^{2} - 4 = 10$

Put~\left(\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2}\right)x^{2} - 4 = u$, then

$u + \dfrac{1}{u} = 10$

$⇒ u^{2} - 10u + 1 = 0$

$⇒ u = \dfrac{10 \pm \sqrt{100 - 4}}{2}$

$⇒ u = 5 \pm \sqrt{24}$

$⇒ u = 5 \pm 2\sqrt{3}\sqrt{2}$

$⇒ u = \left(\sqrt{3} \pm \sqrt{2}\right)2$

$⇒ \left(\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2}\right)x^{2} - 4 = \left(\sqrt{3} \pm \sqrt{2}\right)2$

So,~\left(\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2}\right)x^{2} - 4 = \left(\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2}\right)2$~and~\left(\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2}\right)x^{2} - 4 = \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2}}\right)2$

Therefore,

$x^{2} - 4 = 2 \text{ and } x^{2} - 4 = - 2$

$⇒ x = \pm \sqrt{6} \text{ and } x = \pm \sqrt{2}$

So,~$S = \left\{\sqrt{6}, \sqrt{2}, - \sqrt{6}, - \sqrt{2}\right\}$

Hence,~$n\left(S\right) = 4$

questions.q: Let $S = \left\{x \in R: {\left(\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2}\right)}^{x} + {\left(\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{2}\right)}^{x} = 10\right\}$. Then the number of elements in $S$ is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given: ${\left(\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2}\right)}^{x} + {\left(\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{2}\right)}^{x} = 10$

Now, let ${\left(\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2}\right)}^{x} = t ⇒ {\left(\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{2}\right)}^{x} = \dfrac{1}{t}$

So, ${\left(\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2}\right)}^{x} + {\left(\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{2}\right)}^{x} = 10$

$⇒ t + \dfrac{1}{t} = 10$

$⇒ t^{2} - 10t + 1 = 0$

$⇒ t = 5 \pm 2\sqrt{6}$

$⇒ t = {\left(\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{2}\right)}^{2}, {\left(\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2}\right)}^{2}$

Now, taking ${\left(\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2}\right)}^{x} = {\left(\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{2}\right)}^{2} = {\left(\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2}\right)}^{- 2}$ we get, $x = - 2$

And equating ${\left(\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2}\right)}^{x} = {\left(\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2}\right)}^{2}$ we get, $x = 2$

Hence, the number of elements in $S$ is $2$

So, we can write the given equation as

$3\left[\left(x + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)2 - 2\right] - 2\left(x + \dfrac{1}{x}\right) + 5 = 0$

Let~$x + \dfrac{1}{x} = t$

$⇒ 3\left(t^{2} - 2\right) - 2t + 5 = 0 ⇒ 3t^{2} - 6 - 2t + 5 = 0$

$⇒ 3t^{2} - 2t - 1 = 0 ⇒ 3t^{2} - 3t + t - 1 = 0$

$⇒ 3t\left(t - 1\right) + ( t - 1 ) = 0 ⇒ \left(3t + 1\right)\left(t - 1\right) = 0$

Therefore,~$t = - \dfrac{1}{3}ort = 1$

$CaseI$

$⇒ x^{2} - x + 1 = 0$

$\text{Here}, D = \sqrt{- 3}\text{i.e. no real solution}$

$CaseIIx + \dfrac{1}{x} = - \dfrac{1}{3}$

$⇒ 3x^{2} + x + 3 = 0$

$\text{Here}, D = \sqrt{- 35}\text{i.e. no real solution}$

Hence, we don't have real solutions.

& \left(x^2-9 x+11\right)^2-(x-4)(x-5)=3 \\
& \left(x^2-9 x+11\right)^2-\left(x^2-9 x+20\right)=3

Let $x^2-9 x+11=t$\begin{aligned}
& t^2-(t+9)=3 \\
& \Rightarrow t^2-t-12=0 \\
& \Rightarrow t^2-4 t+3 t-12=0 \\
& \Rightarrow t(t-4)+3(t-4)=0 \\
& \Rightarrow t=4 \text { or }-3 \\
& x^2-9 x+11=4 \\
& x^2-9 x+7=0
\end{aligned}$$
Here, we will get irrational roots
$\begin{aligned}

& \Rightarrow x=7,2 \\
& \Rightarrow \text { Product of all rational roots }=14
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $\alpha$~be a root of the equation $1 + x^{2} + x^{4} = 0$. Then the value of ${α}^{1011} + {α}^{2022} - {α}^{3033}$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,& $x^{4} + x^{2} + 1 = 0$

Using the formula~$a^{4} + a^{2} + 1 = \left(a^{2} + a + 1\right)\left(a^{2} - a + 1\right)$

We get,~\left(x^{2} + x + 1\right)\left($x^{2} - x + 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ x = $\pm \omega, \pm {ω}^{2}~where~\omega = {1}^{1 / 3}~and imaginary.

So~${α}^{1011} + {α}^{2022} - {α}^{3033} = 1 + 1 - 1 = 1

$

questions.q: Let the set $C = \left\{( x, y ) ∣ x^{2} - {2}^{y} = 2023, x, y \in \mathbb{N}\right\}$. Then $\mathop{∑}_{( x, y ) \in C} ( x + y )$ is equal to _______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given

$x^{2} - {2}^{y} = 2023$

$⇒ x^{2} = {2}^{y} + 2023$

Now, if $y = 1$ we get,

$⇒ x^{2} = 2025$

$⇒ x = 45$

And there is no other value which will satisfy the above equation,

Hence, $x = 45 \text{ and } y = 1$

So, $\mathop{∑}_{( x, y ) \in C} ( x + y ) = 45 + 1 = 46$

questions.q: Let $a \in R$ and let $\alpha, \beta$ be the roots of the equation $x^{2} + 60\dfrac{1}{4}x + a = 0$. If ${α}^{4} + {β}^{4} = - 30$, then the product of all possible values of $a$ is _____ .
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Since,& $\alpha, \beta$ be the roots of the equation $x^{2} + 60\dfrac{1}{4}x + a = 0$, therefore

$\alpha + \beta = - 60\dfrac{1}{4}$

$\alpha\beta = a$

Given:

${α}^{4} + {β}^{4} = - 30$

$⇒ \left({α}^{2} + {β}^{2}\right)2 - 2{α}^{2}{β}^{2} = - 30$

$⇒ \left\{\left(\alpha + \beta\right)2 - 2\alpha\beta\right\}2 - 2a^{2} = - 30$

$⇒ \left\{60\dfrac{1}{2} - 2a\right\}2 - 2a^{2} = - 30$

$⇒ 60 + 4a^{2} - 4a \times 60\dfrac{1}{2} - 2a^{2} = - 30$

$⇒ 2a^{2} - 4 \cdot 60\dfrac{1}{2}a + 90 = 0$

$⇒ a^{2} - 2 \cdot 60\dfrac{1}{2}a + 45 = 0$

Product of roots$= 45$

questions.q: The number of real roots of the equation& $e^{4x} - e^{3x} - 4e^{2x} - e^{x} + 1 = 0$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have,& $e^{4x} - e^{3x} - 4e^{2x} - e^{x} + 1 = 0$

Let~$e^{x} = t$, we get

$t^{4} - t^{3} - 4t^{2} - t + 1 = 0$

Divide with~$t^{2}$~on both sides

$⇒ t^{2} - t - 4 - \dfrac{1}{t} + \dfrac{1}{t2} = 0$

$⇒ \left(t + \dfrac{1}{t}\right)2 - \left(t + \dfrac{1}{t}\right) - 6 = 0$

Let~$\alpha = t + \dfrac{1}{t} \ge 2$, we get

${α}^{2} - \alpha - 6 = 0$

$⇒ \left(\alpha - 3\right)\left(\alpha + 2\right) = 0$

$⇒ \alpha = 3, - 2$~(reject)

$⇒ t + \dfrac{1}{t} = 3 ⇒ t^{2} - 3t + 1 = 0$

$⇒ e^{x} = \dfrac{3 \pm \sqrt{5}}{2}$

$⇒ e^{x} = \dfrac{3 \pm 2 . 23}{2} \left(∵ $\sqrt{5} \approx$2 . 23\right)$

$⇒ e^{x} = $\dfrac{5 . 23}{2}~or~$e^{x} = $\dfrac{0 . 77}{2}

$⇒ e^{x} = 2 . 615$~or~$e^{x} = 0 . 385$

$⇒$ The number of real roots $= 2 .

$
